overview: The UIF provides short-term financial relief to workers when they become unemployed, are unable to work due to illness, or take maternity/adoption leave. It also provides benefits to dependants of deceased workers. Contributions are mandatory for all employed persons.

benefits.name: Unemployment Benefits
benefits.description: Paid when you lose your job through retrenchment, dismissal, or contract expiry.
eligibility: You must have been contributing to UIF while employed
You must have been employed for at least 24 months in the last 4 years
You must be actively seeking employment
You must register as a work seeker at your nearest Department of Employment and Labour office
You must NOT have resigned voluntarily (exception: constructive dismissal)
benefit_calculation: Based on a sliding scale: higher earners get a lower percentage
Maximum benefit: 58% of your daily wage (for lowest earners)
Minimum benefit: 38% of your daily wage (for higher earners)
You get 1 day of benefits for every 4 days worked
Benefits are paid monthly via bank transfer
how_to_claim: Step 1: Get your UI-19 form from your employer (this is your discharge certificate — they are LEGALLY REQUIRED to give it to you)
Step 2: Register as a work seeker at your nearest Labour Centre
Step 3: Complete the UI-2.1 (unemployment benefit application) form at the Labour Centre
Step 4: Bring your ID, UI-19 from employer, proof of banking details, proof of registration as work seeker
Step 5: The Labour Centre submits your claim — processing takes 2-6 weeks
Step 6: You must report to the Labour Centre every month to confirm you are still unemployed and seeking work
common_problems: Employer refuses to give UI-19 form — this is illegal. Report them to the Department of Employment and Labour. You can also submit a complaint at your Labour Centre.
Claim takes longer than 6 weeks — escalate at the Labour Centre, ask for the claims manager
Benefits stopped unexpectedly — you may have missed a monthly reporting date. Contact the Labour Centre immediately.
System shows 'no contributions' — your employer may not have been paying UIF contributions (illegal). Report this.

benefits.name: Illness Benefits
benefits.description: Paid when you cannot work due to illness for more than 14 consecutive days.
requirements: A medical certificate from a registered medical practitioner confirming inability to work
You must have exhausted your employer's sick leave
Application must be submitted within 6 months of the first day of illness

benefits.name: Maternity Benefits
benefits.description: Paid to pregnant employees for up to 4 months around the birth.
requirements: You can start claiming up to 4 months before the expected birth date
Must apply at your nearest Labour Centre with your ID, UI-19 from employer, and medical proof of pregnancy
Benefits are 66% of your salary (higher than unemployment benefits)

benefits.name: Adoption Benefits
benefits.description: Paid to the primary caregiver who adopts a child under 2 years old.
requirements: Apply at your Labour Centre with adoption order and employer UI-19

benefits.name: Dependants Benefits
benefits.description: Paid to the dependants (spouse/children) of a deceased contributor.
requirements: Proof of dependency (marriage certificate, children's birth certificates)

labour_centres_ethekwini.name: Labour Centre Durban
labour_centres_ethekwini.tip: Extremely busy. Arrive before 07:00. Bring all documents — if anything is missing you will be sent away and lose your queue position.

online_services.uFiling: www.ufiling.co.za — Check claim status, submit documents, register as work seeker online
online_services.note: The uFiling system is frequently offline or slow. If you cannot access it, visit a Labour Centre in person.

escalation.step_1: Ask to speak with the claims manager at your Labour Centre
escalation.step_3: Lodge a complaint with the Commission for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration (CCMA): 011 377 6650
escalation.step_4: Lodge a complaint with the Public Protector: 0800 11 20 40
escalation.legislation: Unemployment Insurance Act 63 of 2001 and the Unemployment Insurance Contributions Act 4 of 2002

your_rights: Your employer MUST register you for UIF and pay monthly contributions — failure to do so is a criminal offence under the UIA
Your employer MUST provide you with a UI-19 (discharge certificate) when your employment ends — refusal is illegal
UIF must process your claim within a reasonable timeframe
You are entitled to written reasons for any rejection
Domestic workers are covered by UIF — employers of domestic workers must register and contribute
Foreign nationals who contribute to UIF are entitled to claim benefits
employer_obligations: Register all employees for UIF within 30 days of starting employment
Deduct 1% of employee's salary as UIF contribution
Contribute an additional 1% as the employer's share
Submit monthly returns and payments to the UIF
Provide UI-19 discharge certificates when employment ends
